failure.interpretation: The resident preserved the raw operator gap and component admissions, but treated the explicit full-pointer null branch as if it would null admitted object/version components. It chose the repaired_or_unknown branch while its prose claimed an unrepaired non-admitted outcome.

proven: The multi-registry compatibility gate works for most cases under harness-parsed closed branch selection.
Component existence alone did not cause full pointer admission in the PROJECT/ui.menu compatibility-block case.
Version gaps blocked full pointer admission without nearest-version repair in ui.modal@v2 and ui.menu@v2 cases.
gpt-5.4-mini passed all seven cases in the bounded branch-selection role.
not_proven: That the current full-pointer null branch wording is unambiguous under operator-gap cases.
That residents reliably distinguish full pointer null from component nulling without an explicit separate component-preservation branch.
That larger registries or hidden D-law binding will remain stable.
architecture_read: Probe 020 confirms the next D-law: full pointer admission requires component admission, operator-object compatibility, and task-phase admissibility. It also shows that full-pointer non-admission should be represented separately from component nulling and from repaired/unknown pointer states.
recommended_next_probe: Probe 021 should isolate the DELETE/operator-gap failure with split fields: full_pointer_admission = admitted/not_admitted, full_pointer_non_admission_reason = operator_registry_gap, and component_preservation branches for object/version. This should test whether residents stop treating full pointer null as erasing admitted components.
